skills.title: Derive Topology from Map Edges
skills.when_to_apply: When identifying adjacency, reconstructing the local graph, or building candidate routes.
skills.procedure: Determine connections edge by edge strictly from the continuous lines drawn in the map image. Travelmap graphs are undirected (bidirectional) networks of scenic routes; trace each drawn polyline from node endpoint to node endpoint rather than assuming spatial proximity, row order, or external geographic knowledge implies a connection.
skills.check: Every consecutive pair of spots must be connected by one direct visible line segment on the map without skipping intermediate labeled icons or inventing imaginary shortcuts between degree-1 leaf nodes.
skills.source_text:
Derive Topology from Map Edges
When to apply: When identifying adjacency, reconstructing the local graph, or building candidate routes.
Procedure: Determine connections edge by edge strictly from the continuous lines drawn in the map image. Travelmap graphs are undirected (bidirectional) networks of scenic routes; trace each drawn polyline from node endpoint to node endpoint rather than assuming spatial proximity, row order, or external geographic knowledge implies a connection.
Check: Every consecutive pair of spots must be connected by one direct visible line segment on the map without skipping intermediate labeled icons or inventing imaginary shortcuts between degree-1 leaf nodes.

skills.title: Expand Every Traversed Spot
skills.when_to_apply: When tracing a route through a chain, branch, intersection, bend, or visually dense region.
skills.procedure: Follow the chosen through-path continuously from spot to spot and record every labeled spot on that through-path, ensuring intermediate nodes situated along the line (e.g. transit stations, landmarks) are included. At each junction, distinguish trunk through-corridors from terminal side branches/dead ends (degree-1 leaf nodes connected only to that junction); never treat a leaf node as a through-bridge or insert a dead-end spur unless it is the designated start or destination.
skills.check: Do not skip a visible intermediate spot on the path, insert a dead-end spur that requires backtracking, reverse route order, or invent non-existent connections.

skills.title: Normalize Spot Names
skills.when_to_apply: When the map and Vertex Table use aliases, abbreviations, translations, punctuation, or similar-looking names.
skills.procedure: Use map position and neighboring spots to match each map node to exactly one canonical Vertex Table entry. Use that table name consistently in calculations and final output.
skills.check: Never attach one spot's attributes to another spot or treat two spellings of the same spot as separate vertices.

skills.title: Separate Map Topology from Table Attributes
skills.when_to_apply: Whenever determining adjacency and retrieving numerical attributes.
skills.procedure: Use the map image only to establish direct connections and route order. Use the Vertex Table only to retrieve the four attributes after a spot has been identified.
skills.check: Table row order does not imply map adjacency, and numerical similarity does not create an edge.

skills.title: Enumerate Structurally Distinct Candidates
skills.when_to_apply: When branches, cycles, crossings, or multiple connecting corridors may provide different legal routes.
skills.procedure: Construct the principal structurally distinct loop-free candidates supported by visible edges. Include alternatives that could plausibly change the weighted decision, but omit routes that are merely long cyclic detours.
skills.check: Do not select the route solely because it has the fewest spots, looks most direct, or is the first route noticed.

skills.title: Distinguish Unique and Multi-Path Topologies
skills.when_to_apply: After the initial topology inspection and before numerical scoring.
skills.procedure: Determine whether exactly one legal simple route exists. If so, retain that route and state the concrete topological reason. If alternatives exist, compare the principal legal candidates.
skills.check: Do not invent alternatives for a unique path or declare a route unique before checking visible branches and reconnections.

skills.title: Compute Weighted Cost Consistently
skills.when_to_apply: After the legal candidate routes have been fixed.
skills.procedure: For every candidate, compute `T`, `P`, `C`, and `R` to 6 decimal places with the authoritative formula. Show each individual weighted product term (`w_i * metric`) before summing them to obtain the final `RouteScore` (to 6 decimal places).
skills.check: Use identical scaling, precision, and attribute scope for every candidate. Do not replace the formula with an informal preference or shortest-route heuristic.

skills.title: Include Both Route Endpoints
skills.when_to_apply: When building the attribute list for a candidate route.
skills.procedure: Include the start, every intermediate spot, and the destination in the Time, Price, Comfort Level, and Reliability calculations, subject only to the effective-price and nonzero-average rules.
skills.check: Do not omit either endpoint or use a different spot set for different attributes.
skills.source_text:
Include Both Route Endpoints

Check: Do not omit either endpoint or use a different spot set for different attributes.

skills.title: Average Nonzero Quality Costs
skills.when_to_apply: When calculating Comfort Level and Reliability costs.
skills.procedure: Normalize each nonzero Comfort Level using `Comfort Level/5`, convert it to `1-Comfort Level/5`, and average those costs. Separately convert each nonzero Reliability value to `1-Reliability` and average those costs.
skills.check: Exclude an entry only when its original value for that same quality attribute is zero. Do not sum quality costs without dividing by the correct nonzero count.

skills.title: Apply the Zero-Time Effective-Price Rule
skills.procedure: Set Price to zero only when that zero-Time spot is not the destination. If the zero-Time spot is the destination, retain its original Price. Normalize the resulting effective prices by 200.
skills.check: Do not erase the destination's Price, retain an intermediate transport hub's Price, or omit its other nonzero attributes.
skills.source_text:
Apply the Zero-Time Effective-Price Rule
When to apply: Whenever any route spot has `Time = 0`.
Procedure: Set Price to zero only when that zero-Time spot is not the destination. If the zero-Time spot is the destination, retain its original Price. Normalize the resulting effective prices by 200.
Check: Do not erase the destination's Price, retain an intermediate transport hub's Price, or omit its other nonzero attributes.

skills.title: Recheck Close Candidate Scores
skills.when_to_apply: When two candidates have close totals, when different components favor different routes, or when one weight dominates the objective.
skills.procedure: Recompute the component sums, quality averages, effective prices, weighted products, and final addition for the competing candidates before deciding.
skills.check: A dominant weight guides attention but does not replace the complete weighted calculation. Every ranking claim must cite numerical scores.

skills.title: Validate Every Edge Before Scoring
skills.when_to_apply: Before admitting a candidate to numerical comparison.
skills.procedure: Verify the requested start and destination, each consecutive map edge, every intermediate spot, and the absence of repeated spots or edges.
skills.check: Reject candidates containing an invented edge, skipped spot, wrong endpoint, repeated spot, repeated edge, or loop.

skills.title: Perform a Final Audit of the Best Candidate
skills.when_to_apply: After identifying the current minimum-score candidate.
skills.procedure: Audit the complete route, its table lookups, effective-price decisions, averaging denominators, weighted score, and agreement between the reasoning and final route.
skills.check: If any item fails, correct the calculation or choose another validated candidate before answering.

skills.title: Output the Complete Canonical Route
skills.when_to_apply: Once the best legal route has been established.
skills.procedure: Output the start, every intermediate spot, and the destination in travel order using canonical Vertex Table names joined by hyphens.
skills.check: Do not omit spots, translate names, add explanations inside the route, or place spaces around separators.

skills.title: Prioritize a Complete Response
skills.when_to_apply: When the route is known or the remaining output budget is limited.
skills.procedure: Always finish one complete `<reasoning>...</reasoning>` block followed immediately by one complete `<response>...</response>` block. Compress secondary explanation before sacrificing the final route.
skills.check: Never return a truncated route, an empty block, a missing closing tag, or extra text outside the two required blocks.
